learning: No race telemetry for this geometry yet. Next race should show whether the wider spread cuts line-loss events, and whether kp 3.5 with kd 0.4 avoids oscillation on the lighter, narrower robot.
notes: Complete runnable robot for the Builder's wider-spread, narrower-track, lighter drivetrain geometry. Sensor weights are rescaled to the ±0.036 m spread and kp is raised to keep the per-metre steering gain near the baseline. Outcome is not yet measured.
rationale: The baseline (iteration 0) reached the 0.06 m off-track limit on all 60 trials. Max error averaged about 0.06 m and line-loss events averaged 1.0 to 1.35 per run, so the tape was lost at the edge of the 0.048 m sensor span. The Builder's geometry for this iteration widens the span to ±0.036 m and changes the drivetrain to a 0.10 m track, 0.035 m wheels and 0.6 kg mass. The sensor weights must be rescaled to match the new spread: the weight of each sensor is its lateral position divided by 0.018 m and clipped to [-2, 2], which gives [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. The signal per metre of tape offset falls by about one third, and the narrower track raises turn rate per unit of wheel difference by about 20 percent. To keep the per-metre steering gain close to the baseline, kp is raised from 3.0 to 3.5 (about 3.75 by the exact ratio, reduced slightly to limit overshoot on the lighter robot). kd is raised modestly from 0.3 to 0.4 to damp the faster yaw response. ki stays at 0.05 to avoid windup. base_speed stays at 1.6 so this iteration isolates the geometry change. line_loss stays at last_direction, which suited the baseline. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and a lower max_error on the s-bend and slalom. Whether steering oscillates is untested.
